event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_baite: You lean low enough to cut the sack away before the hit. A tooth or hook catches you in the attempt.
You wrench the hull out of the attack line. The predator only bites the outer planking.
You force the boat to cross its own bait trail. The predator changes target, but the hard turn costs timber.
A pirate boat races past and throws a sack of bloody meat against your hull. A large fin immediately turns toward the scent while the raiders accelerate away.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_black: You let the sloop close, then break the angle sharply. A shot catches you during the maneuver, but their close-range trap fails.
You throw the money in a weighted bag. The pirates recover it and let you pass.
You refuse. The next volley bites into your planking before the two ships separate.
A black-flag sloop cuts across your path and fires a warning shot. Its captain names a price: two thousand Berrys now, or the next volley goes into the hull.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_board: Cut the net at the center
The net collapses. Two pirates fall, but the third crashes onto your deck tangled in the mesh.
You drop the caught yard with the net. It takes part of the rig with it.
You give up the foredeck and receive the first attackers from a defensive position.
A net cannon cracks from a pirate schooner. The weighted mesh catches between your mast and theirs, and three attackers are already sliding down the taut lines.
You cut the mesh caught in the rail. A few fittings go with it.
You pin him under the mesh while the schooner falls away.
You cinch the mesh around the attacker until he drops his weapon.
The fallen raider thrashes in the net at your feet. Behind him, the schooner hauls on the mesh to recover him along with anything still caught in it.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_bomb_: Spot the short fuses
Detonate the nearest one
Thread between the barrels
Two barrels detonate almost together against the hull and throw you down.
You clear the line without a close blast. One barrel remains snagged on a chain behind the stern.
You avoid the heart of the blast, but one barrel bursts close enough to open the planking.
You set off one barrel before it reaches the hull. The blast triggers a second one too close.
You clear the barrel line. A chain is still dragging behind the stern: one last barrel is hooked to it.
A pirate sloop drops five barrels astern. Each carries a lit fuse and drifts into your widening wake: they are not floating at random, they are closing off your route.
Fuse Barrels
Cut the chain at full reach
Haul it within reach
Swing it far astern
You stretch the chain out and cut it. The barrel drifts free, but the fuse is nearly gone.
You haul the barrel close enough to reach it. Only a few centimeters of fuse remain.
You use the chain like a pendulum and throw the barrel farther astern. The fuse is almost down to the hoop.
The last barrel bounces in your wake, held by a chain snagged under the stern. Its fuse keeps getting shorter.
The Tethered Barrel
Douse the fuse
Kick it farther away
Shield the stern
You reach the fuse with enough water to kill it at the last second.
You gain just enough distance. The blast stuns you but spares the hull.
You present the strongest part of the stern. The blast tears out a fitting, not the whole hull.
The fuse is now only a red thread. The barrel is finally clear of the stern, but still close enough to hit hard if it blows now.
A Few Seconds
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_burni: Seal it and starve the fire
You flood the locker before the fire catches. Water and heat damage part of the inner planking.
You seal the hatch. The fire runs out of air, but works the timber before dying.
You smother the fire at close range. Heat punches through the blanket and burns your forearms.
After an enemy shot, a burning cannon wad drops through the hatch and rolls into a locker of dry rope. Black smoke is already pushing up through the planks.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_chain: Drop the sail
Muscle the chain loose
Free the yards
Send the shipwright
The shipwright slips with the yard and is badly hurt before the chain gives.
The shipwright frees the rig cleanly and keeps the yard under control.
The shipwright hurts an arm and frees only part of the rig.
The shipwright drops the chain, but the split yard remains hanging.
The chain cinches tighter. The mast tears out fittings and throws you onto the deck.
You free the rig before the second volley. A split yard still hangs by one halyard.
You sacrifice the damaged sail. The mast stops pulling, but the ship takes the brutal maneuver.
You buy a few seconds, but the sail still pulls and the planking groans dangerously.
The chain drops, but a split yard still hangs over the deck.
A chain shot wraps around the yards with a sharp crack. The sail pulls sideways while the enemy ship reloads: if the mast goes, the hull will follow.
Chain in the Rigging
Clear only the helm
Drop it overboard
Lash it to the mast
You shove the yard clear of the helm. The deck takes the hit instead.
You cut the right halyard and the yard drops into the sea clear of the helm.
You lash it against the mast. The rig remains usable, but under strain.
The split yard swings over the deck while the enemy ship turns for another pass. If it falls in the wrong place, it will jam the helm.
The Hanging Yard
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_elect: Let go of all metal
Give the passage to the navigator
Read the pulse pattern
Thread between the lights
The navigator takes the helm at the wrong moment and catches a violent shock directly.
The navigator crosses with almost no contact; only one jelly remains on the chain.
The navigator finds a way out but takes several shocks while holding the helm.
The navigator finds a gap. One jellyfish still sticks to the rudder chain.
A heavy discharge runs through the deck and the hull hits the field head-on.
You pass through almost untouched. One jellyfish remains stuck to the rudder chain, still charged.
You clear the field, but several shocks hit before you are out.
You abandon the helm until the strongest pulse passes. The ship drifts and clips several jellies.
You reach thinner water. One jellyfish remains stuck against the rudder chain and is still charging it.
A field of electric jellyfish lights up beneath the hull. Every contact sends a charge through the wet fittings, and the helm has begun to vibrate under your hands.
The Sea Crackles
Sacrifice a chain link
Knock it loose with rope
Wait for the low pulse
You cut one link and isolate the charged section. The rudder is left with some play.
You knock it loose with a wet rope. One last shock runs up into your hands.
You wait for the glow to fade, then clear the chain without damage.
The jelly stuck to the rudder keeps pulsing. Each contraction sends a spark along the metal chain beneath the helm.
The Charged Chain
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_firep: A pot bursts against you and fire bites into the sail before it is contained.
You smother almost all the fire. The smoke still reveals a pirate skiff using it as cover.
You cut away the burning canvas before it takes the mast. The ship loses part of its rig.
You limit the blaze, but flame and shards still catch you.
The flames die down. Through the smoke, a small pirate skiff is already at your stern.
Clay firepots burst across the deck. The pirates stay out of reach and aim for the rigging: a few seconds will turn the sails into torches.
You cut the line holding the skiff against you. It falls away, tearing out a fitting.
You force the carrier to drop the pot into his own skiff. He falls back cursing.
You knock the ladder away before it catches the rail.
The pirate skiff bumps your stern. Two men raise a ladder while a third readies another firepot.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_grapp: Take the boarding
Cut the grapples
Pick off the climbers
You let the first pirates land and drive them back hand to hand. You keep the deck, but not without blood.
The lines hold. Two pirates hit you as they land and a third tears away a purse before falling back.
You break the boarding rush. One last pirate jumps anyway, cut off from the rest of the crew.
You slow the boarding, but a blade opens your side while a hook tears loose a plank.
Most lines fall. One pirate still manages to swing onto the deck.
Three grappling hooks bite into the rail. A pirate brig closes alongside and figures are already running the lines: if they gain the deck, they will go for the helm and your money.
Hooks Bite
Cut his retreat
Rush him now
Keep the helm between you
You sever his escape line. The pirate drops his weapon to cling to the rail.
You drive him back to the rail. His line stays taut between the two ships.
You force him to circle the helm until he loses his angle on you.
The last raider lands beside the helm. He hesitates between striking you and cutting the line still tying him to the brig.
One Raider on Deck
Let the rail go
Pin the line to a cleat
Grab and cut it
You sacrifice the already-split section. It leaves with the line, but the rest of the hull holds.
You pin the line just long enough to slacken it and cast it loose cleanly.
The line burns your palms before dropping into the sea.
The pirate brig starts to peel away. The last taut line whips across the deck, threatening to sweep someone overboard or tear out more rail.
The Last Line
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_harpo: Sacrifice the bowsprit
Ride its pull
Free the line
The line snaps taut. The bowsprit cracks and you are thrown against the rail.
You regain control of the pull. The sea bull surfaces just under the bow, still trapped by the line.
You cut away the trapped section before the animal takes more with it. The hull is saved, not the forward rig.
You reduce the pull, but the line still saws into the timber before shifting.
You give the line slack. The animal surfaces under the bow, still tied to the harpoon and your rig.
A huge sea bull surges beneath your bow with a harpoon in its shoulder. The line has snagged under your bowsprit, and the panicked animal is now dragging your ship sideways.
The Harpooned Sea Bull
Break the harpoon shaft
Cut the harpoon line
Slip the line free
You break the shaft to free the animal. The released line instantly snaps back toward the deck.
You cut behind the harpoon. The animal dives and the loose section whips back toward the deck.
You work the line out of the rig without pulling the wound. Its full length suddenly comes whipping back up.
The sea bull blows at the surface. The harpoon is still through its shoulder and the line now passes within reach, though it is not fully slack.
Under the Bow
Let the fitting tear free
Pin it under a boot
Catch it bare-handed
You let the line tear out a fitting instead of taking your legs.
You pin the line as it passes and it falls dead before building speed again.
You stop the line, but it burns deep into your palms.
The long wet line lashes across the deck at shin height. One bad step is enough to drag someone toward the rail.
The Line Whips Back
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_knife: You sacrifice the already-cut line to keep the saboteurs away from the rest.
The lines nearly give at once and a saboteur strikes you from the water when you lean over the rail.
You save the rudder lines. One saboteur, cut off from his boat, still surfaces against the rail.
You disrupt them, but they cut enough line to leave the helm dangerously loose.
You drive the swimmers out from under the stern. One still surfaces at the rail, knife in hand.
Two trails of bubbles follow your stern. Underwater saboteurs are sawing at the rudder lines while an enemy boat stays just out of reach.
You cut the small recovery line tying him to the boat. Both saboteurs are forced to disengage.
He drops the knife and falls back into the water before the boat returns.
You wrench the weapon away, but the blade opens your forearm.
The saboteur grips the rail with one hand and raises a knife with the other. His boat is already turning back to recover him.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_lit_k: You cut the visible fuse. A second glow appears under the keg hoop.
You keep the keg from falling below deck, but the blast catches you in the open.
The keg explodes against the hull before sinking far enough away.
A fleeing raider shoves a small powder keg onto your deck before jumping overboard. The fuse is already burning and the keg is rolling toward the hatch.
You drown the keg until the fuse dies beneath the hoop.
You tear off the hoop in time, but the metal cuts your hands.
You drive it away from the vital areas. The blast still tears out a few planks.
The second fuse disappears under an iron hoop. The keg cannot be opened cleanly before it reaches the powder.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_mast_: Cross under cover
Stay below the rail
Give the shot to the gunner
Look for the glint
The gunner exposes themself and takes the shot while searching for the target.
The countershot cleanly drives the marksman from the perch; the stay is his only escape.
The gunner is hit while forcing the marksman to move.
The gunner forces the marksman out of position and down toward your side.
The second shot hits you before you find the marksman.
You break his angle immediately. The marksman abandons the perch and makes a desperate slide toward your side.
You leave the helm for a few seconds to stay out of his line. The marksman loses the shot, but you lose the initiative too.
You move enough to avoid the worst, but a round still cuts you.
You force the marksman out of his perch. He is now sliding down a stay toward your side.
A shot tears through your sleeve and hits the helm. On the passing ship, a marksman is hidden in the rigging and is already looking for a second line of sight.
Shot from the Mast
Cut the stay
Meet him at the rail
Shake the line
You cut the stay before he reaches your side.
You meet him at the rail and force him to let go, taking a hit in the exchange.
You shake the stay until he chooses to slide back toward his own ship.
The marksman slides along a stay stretched between the two ships. In seconds, he can drop onto your deck or swing back to his own.
The Marksman Comes Down
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_ram_s: The ram hits broadside and throws you hard against the deck.
You break its charge. The skiff only slides along the stern, too close to disengage cleanly.
You lessen the impact, but the skiff tears planking as it scrapes past.
The ram misses center mass. The skiff still scrapes your stern and stays within pole reach.
You give them the stern instead of the broadside. The hit costs timber, but not the whole hull.
An armored skiff turns hard and points its ram at your flank. Its crew is not trying to sink you; they want to pin you long enough to board.
You sacrifice the section of rail caught by the hook and the skiff loses its grip.
You shove their bow with everything that bears. The skiff finally breaks away.
You lever against the rail and the pole snaps cleanly.
The skiff scrapes your stern. A pirate drives a long hooked pole into the rail while the others prepare to haul the two hulls together.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_razor: You drop the line whipping across the deck. The wave passes, but the rig loses a useful section.
You raise canvas and the second wave buries itself in it. The school is already turning for another pass.
You flatten yourself. The fins pass overhead, but one cuts you as it falls.
A school of flying fish with razor-edged fins bursts from the water at deck height. The first wave cuts lines; the second is coming straight at your faces.
You beat them aside as they pass, but a fin opens your shoulder.
You kill the bright reflections and the school passes wide.
You let a strip of canvas flap away from the helm. The school shreds it instead of coming back at you.
The school wheels around the mast and comes back lower, drawn to the bright flashes of the wet rigging.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_shell: You cut lines that might snag on the shell. The rig comes out of it lighter.
You let the ship slide across the shell. You keep your footing, but the keel scrapes hard.
You shift your weight too quickly and fall, but the ship regains its balance.
The sea bulges beneath the keel. A gigantic sea turtle rises directly under your ship and lifts one side of the deck; loose barrels and lines are already sliding toward the rail.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_spike: You strike the chain as it passes. It breaks, but the spikes whip you before dropping away.
You kill your speed before contact. The chain passes ahead, but the boats rake you with gunfire as you back down.
You give the chain an angle to slide along. It still tears out several planks before falling free.
Two pirate boats cross ahead of your bow with a heavy spiked chain stretched between them. It is already rising toward your planking like a giant saw.
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_squid: Cut whatever holds you
Have the fighter pull
Pry the suckers loose
Slip the coil
The fighter takes the pull head-on and the tentacle slams them into the deck.
The fighter breaks the hold in one heave. The second arm still drops onto the capstan.
The fighter pulls you free but is hurt under the strain.
The fighter tears you free. The second arm reaches the capstan.
The tentacle crushes you against the rail and tears timber loose as it tightens.
You break free cleanly and stay on your feet. The second tentacle still wraps around the capstan.
You free yourself by sacrificing line and fittings caught with the tentacle.
You partly break free, but the suckers rake you before releasing.
You escape the first arm. The second is now coiling around the capstan.
A giant squid arm lashes across the deck and coils around your waist. The suckers pull you toward the rail while a second tentacle reaches for the capstan.
An Arm Across the Deck
Dump the lines
Sacrifice the capstan
Trap the arm under a hatch
You cast off the lines and the tentacle loses its leverage on the capstan.
You clear the last lines and let the capstan tear free before the whole deck follows.
You slam a heavy hatch across the arm. It withdraws, but the recoil catches you.
The second tentacle cinches around the capstan and starts pulling the lines with it. If it tears free, the deck will open around the bolts.
The Capstan Caught
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_water: Drive in a timber wedge
Find the true breach
Seal the compartment
Let the shipwright patch it
The shipwright is hit by a failed brace and the breach opens wider.
The shipwright seals the leak cleanly before the second shot.
The shipwright is hurt holding a patch that still leaks.
The shipwright shores up the breach. The enemy gun is already firing again.
The breach opens wider under pressure and throws you into a frame.
You seal the leak cleanly. The second gun still fires before you clear the angle.
You slow the flooding, but the improvised patch does not take the full strain.
You isolate the section and accept the water already inside. The ship stays afloat but badly hurt.
The leak is contained. The enemy gun is already firing again.
A cannonball punches in below the waterline. Water is already hammering the frames while the enemy ship adjusts to fire a second shot at the same spot.
Hole Below the Line
Heel the ship
Show the stern
Hold course
You briefly lift the damaged area above the waterline, at the cost of brutal strain on the rig.
You swing the ship and the shot misses the patch.
You hold course. The shot lands higher and splinters rake you.
The patch holds, but the second shot is coming for the same strip of hull. You only have time to present another angle or take it.
The Second Shot
event.active_generic_sea_03_danger_wreck: The first volley catches you and shots tear splinters from the planking.
You ruin their angle. The raiders are left with one hurried grappling hook to try to hold you.
You get out of their best angle, but not before several hits.
You force the shooters to duck, but your deck still takes splinters.
You break their line of fire. A grappling hook immediately flies from the wreck toward your rail.
A half-sunk wreck drifts abeam. Muzzle flashes suddenly blink between its ribs: raiders hidden inside are using the carcass as a floating fort.
You cut the line before it fully comes taut.
You use their own line to swing the wreck sideways and ruin their firing angles for good.
You tear the grapple free with part of the already-split rail.
The grapple catches the rail. The raiders haul from the wreck, trying to pull you back into their firing angle.
